title: Granola Email Integration: Turn Meeting Notes Into Follow-Ups
summary: Connect your Granola email integration to Slashy to draft follow-up emails using full meeting context. Sync notes, summaries, and action items…
body_markdown:
Founders spend hours translating scribbled meeting notes into follow-up emails that actually close deals. The friction isn't just the writing. It's the context switching between a note-taking app like Granola and the inbox. When you have to copy and paste summaries to remind yourself what a prospect actually said, you lose the momentum of the call. Granola is excellent for capturing what happened, but it usually stays trapped in its own silo.


Slashy acts as a data layer between your notes and your communication. By using Slashy's memory system, you bring your previous communication context directly into your email client. The AI can then draft replies that reference specific details from your conversation, not just the text in the email thread. Before you begin, make sure you have the Slashy desktop or mobile app installed.


## Step 1: Configure Slashy Settings


Open Settings with Cmd+, and go to Integrations, then Meeting Notes, then Granola. Click Connect Granola and you are sent to Granola to sign in. Grant Slashy access to your meeting notes, and you land back in Slashy with notes syncing in the background.


That connection is the groundwork for[AI email for sales teams](https://www.slashy.com/blog/ai-email-for-sales-teams-2026) , where context is what separates a fast reply from a good one. There is no browser extension to install.


## Step 2: Let the Memory System Process Your History


The first sync after connecting pulls your full Granola history, not just meetings going forward, so give it a few minutes to backfill before you go looking for older events. Separately from the note sync, Slashy's memory system learns your writing voice so drafts read like you rather than like a template.


Meetings are matched by the event's calendar identifier, so a call that gets rescheduled in Google Calendar still pairs correctly on both sides. While the backfill runs you can keep using the[AI meeting scheduler from email](https://www.slashy.com/blog/ai-meeting-scheduler-from-email-book-calls-without-the-back-and-forth) to book new calls.


## Step 3: Access Context Inside Calendar Events


Visibility is the main benefit of this integration. You no longer need to toggle between apps to prep for a follow-up. In Slashy, a calendar lives directly alongside the inbox. Open any calendar event that was recorded in Granola and the notes appear in the event detail panel, alongside attendees, location and the video link.


This integration solves the problem of meeting amnesia. Before you open an unread email from a prospect, you can glance at the sidebar to see exactly what you promised them. Slashy helps you prioritize your response based on the actual conversation context. From there the agent can reference those notes when you ask it to prep a related meeting or draft the follow-up. It is the same shape as the[Attio email integration](https://www.slashy.com/blog/guides/attio-email-integration-log-deals-from-your-inbox-automatically) : the record lives in the other tool, and the inbox is where you act on it.


## Step 4: Know What Syncs, and in Which Direction


Notes flow both ways, but not every field does. Meeting title, time and attendees come from Granola into Slashy. Summary and notes sync in both directions, and so do action items, so a note you write on an event in Slashy turns up in Granola the next time you open that meeting.


The return leg is the part most people never set up, and it is where the record stops going stale. The useful detail often arrives after the call rather than during it: a prospect names a budget in a reply, or flags the security review that has to happen first. Write that onto the event in Slashy and Granola has it before your next meeting, instead of holding a record that stopped the moment the call ended.


## Step 5: Draft a Follow-Up Email Using Meeting Context


The actual follow-up is where Slashy's memory system delivers the most value. Ask the agent to draft the follow-up and it works from the summary and action items already on that event, alongside your email and your existing memories. Because it has per-recipient memory, the draft opens from what you actually discussed rather than from "Thanks for the chat."


If the draft is not right, say what to change in the same plain language you used to ask for it. If Slashy's memory system indicates a casual relationship with a contact, the draft will reflect that. Follow-up time drops from minutes to seconds. You review the draft and click send. This workflow is particularly effective for founder-led sales where personal touch is required but time is limited. Using your actual conversation data, Slashy creates emails that read as human and researched.


One limit is worth knowing up front: notes attached to events you were not invited to do not sync. Only meetings on your connected calendars are eligible, which keeps other people's calendars out of your inbox.


Privacy and security are taken seriously throughout this process. Slashy is SOC 2 Type II certified and CASA Tier 2 certified. User data is never used to train AI models. The AI providers Slashy uses guarantee zero data retention. For founders handling sensitive deal information, that matters. For more details, verify the current security protocols in the guide on[is it safe to give AI access to your email](https://www.slashy.com/blog/is-it-safe-to-give-an-ai-assistant-access-to-your-email) .


## Troubleshooting and What to Do Next


If notes are not appearing, confirm the meeting sat on a calendar you have connected and that you were an invitee, since events you were not invited to are not eligible to sync.


If an older meeting is still missing, check that the first backfill has finished before assuming anything is wrong. Slashy starts with 7 days of full access, which is long enough to run a week of real follow-ups off synced notes and judge whether the drafts hold up.


## Conclusion


Slashy's automated workflows remove the manual work of turning conversations into communication. By bringing your communication history into a unified inbox, you give Slashy the full history of your relationships to work with. You stop guessing what you promised and stop searching through separate accounts to find context. Your notes become active assets that move deals forward rather than static files in a database.


If you want to stop copy-pasting and start using your context to close more deals, try Slashy today. Slashy's memory system will start learning from your writing voice immediately, building a voice-accurate drafting experience that saves hours every week. Switch to Slashy and put your memory system to work in every follow-up you send.
